headline: High-risk default interaction: shared filesystem plus broad shell/network access creates prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and B explicitly shares state via filesystem while A uses workflow files and stdin/stdout. That creates a default content-bridging path where attacker-controlled files from A can influence B’s interpretation. No shared MCP is shown, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF A writes untrusted workflow/output files into a directory B reads
IF B ingests file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories
Disable automatic file ingestion in B
Add a manual review step before B reads A outputs
Use read-only mounts for A outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while B can access the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress. In the default pair, sensitive data can flow from A into B and then out through B’s model-provider calls or other network actions. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF A processes secrets, logs, database data, or cloud storage data
IF B reads any A-produced files and sends context to a remote model provider
mitigations: Restrict B to a scrubbed workspace
Block network egress for B during sensitive runs
Redact secrets from A outputs before handoff
Use separate OS users for A and B
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A and B both have filesystem write, shell execution, and subprocess spawning; B also modifies git state and shares state via filesystem. Concurrent runs can overwrite each other’s artifacts or git changes without locking, making destructive conflicts plausible in default multi-instance use. The overlap is broad enough for high severity.
conditions: IF A and B run concurrently against the same directory
IF B modifies git state while A writes artifacts or workflow files
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate working tree
Disable concurrent execution on shared repos
Use filesystem locks around shared outputs
Make B operate on copies, not the live repo
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate workflow artifacts, logs, and notifications, and B can act on local files and execute shell commands. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, A’s mistakes can cascade into B’s actions with real side effects. Because B has arbitrary code execution and network access, the downstream blast radius is high.
conditions: IF B consumes A-produced files or messages as trusted inputs
IF B executes commands derived from A outputs without verification
mitigations: Require human approval before B acts on A outputs
Add schema validation for A-produced artifacts
Log and diff A outputs before execution
Limit B to read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: A handles workflow, logs, database, cloud-storage, messages, and notifications; B can access anything reachable on the local machine and has clipboard/files access. If regulated data is present, the pair can move it into a broader local-desktop automation surface without documented residency or retention controls. The mismatch is compliance-relevant but not provably a residency breach from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII or PHI is present in A’s inputs or outputs
IF B copies or stores that data on the local machine or clipboard
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs
Disable clipboard use for sensitive tasks
Use a dedicated compliant workstation
Set short retention on A outputs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
